why: ab = down, off: put it down and leave it, or switch a machine off.
ex: Ich stelle das Fahrrad im Hof ab.
exEn: I am leaving the bike in the courtyard.

en: employ; switch on; sich anstellen: queue; etwas anstellen: get up to (mischief)
why: an = on, in contact: a person put "on" the staff (angestellt = employed), yourself put on the end of a queue.
ex: Wir stellen uns an der Kasse an.
exEn: We are queueing at the till.

en: set up, put up; draw up (a list)
why: auf = up: stand something up. A list or a team is set up the same way.
ex: Wir stellen das Zelt am See auf.
exEn: We are putting the tent up by the lake.

why: aus = out: put things out where people can see them. An office puts out a passport.
ex: Das Museum stellt alte Fotos aus.
exEn: The museum is exhibiting old photos.

why: ein = in: put a setting into a device (die Einstellungen = Settings), put a person into a company. "Stop" (die Produktion einstellen) is a separate sense: learn it.
ex: Die Firma stellt drei neue Leute ein.
exEn: The company is hiring three new people.

why: vor = in front: place a person in front of others, or a picture in front of your mind. Ich stelle mich vor (Akk) = I introduce myself; ich stelle mir das vor (Dat) = I imagine it.
exEn: Let me briefly introduce myself.

why: zu = to, and closed: place the parcel at the door, or put things in a doorway until it is blocked.
ex: Der Bote stellt das Paket morgen zu.
exEn: The courier will deliver the parcel tomorrow.

why: um (stressed) = change: put things in a new arrangement.
exEn: We are rearranging the furniture.

why: um (unstressed) = all the way around: stand all around something.
exEn: The police are surrounding the house.

why: Learn it as a word. be- makes the thing you order the direct object: Ich bestelle eine Pizza.
exEn: I am ordering a pizza.

why: ver = off course: a setting moved out of place, a path blocked, a voice that is not your own.
exEn: Who has changed my seat setting?

why: ent = undoing: put out of its true shape.
exEn: The scar disfigures his face.

en: create, draw up (a list, a document)
why: er = to a result: put something together until it exists.
exEn: I am making a list.

en: put down; take off (a coat); take (an exam)
why: ab = off: take your coat off and lay it down. Eine Prüfung ablegen = take an exam: learn it as a phrase.
ex: Ich lege im Oktober die Prüfung ab.
exEn: I am taking the exam in October.

en: create (a file, an account); invest; moor
why: an = on: lay a new file on the pile; a boat lays itself against the quay.
ex: Ich lege einen neuen Ordner an.
exEn: I am creating a new folder.

why: auf = onto: lay the receiver back onto its cradle.
exEn: He just hangs up.

en: put in, insert; eine Pause einlegen: take a break
why: ein = in: lay something into something else.
ex: Wir legen eine kurze Pause ein.
exEn: We are taking a short break.

why: vor = in front: lay it in front of someone.
ex: Bitte legen Sie Ihren Ausweis vor.
exEn: Please show your ID.

en: put more on (a fire); add more
why: nach = after: lay more on after the first.
exEn: I am putting more wood on.

en: sich etwas zulegen: get yourself something; gain (weight, speed)
why: zu = added: lay more onto what you have.
ex: Ich lege mir ein neues Fahrrad zu.
exEn: I am getting myself a new bike.

why: über = over: turn a question over in your mind. (überlegen as an adjective means superior.)
exEn: I am still thinking about it.

en: fill (a roll); take (a course); prove (with evidence)
why: be- aims at a target: lay something on a surface. Ein belegtes Brötchen has something laid on it; a seat that is belegt is taken.
exEn: I am taking a German course.

en: move, postpone (to another time or place); misplace
why: ver = away, off course: lay it somewhere else, on purpose or by mistake. (verlegen as an adjective means embarrassed.)
ex: Wir verlegen das Treffen auf Freitag.
exEn: We are moving the meeting to Friday.

why: zer = to pieces.
exEn: He is taking the old wardrobe apart.

en: drop off (a passenger); take off (a hat)
why: ab = off: set someone down off the car.
ex: Ich setze dich am Bahnhof ab.
exEn: I will drop you off at the station.

why: an = at: set a meeting at a time.
ex: Wir setzen das Treffen für Montag an.
exEn: We are scheduling the meeting for Monday.

en: put on (glasses, a hat); draft (a letter)
why: auf = onto: set it on your head.
exEn: I am putting my glasses on.

en: stop for a moment, cut out (an engine); abandon (an animal)
why: aus = out: set out of action.
exEn: The engine sometimes cuts out.

en: insert; use; sich einsetzen für: stand up for
why: ein = in: set something into place; set yourself into a cause.
ex: Sie setzt sich für den Tierschutz ein.
exEn: She campaigns for animal welfare.

why: um = change: set an idea over into reality.
ex: Wir setzen den Plan sofort um.
exEn: We are putting the plan into practice at once.

why: über (unstressed) = over: set a text over into another language.
exEn: I am translating the letter.

why: über (stressed) = across: set people over to the other bank.
ex: Die Fähre setzt uns ans andere Ufer über.
exEn: The ferry takes us across to the other bank.

en: push through; sich durchsetzen: get your way
why: durch = through: push through against resistance.
exEn: She usually gets her way.

why: be- aims at a target: set people onto a place, so it is occupied.
exEn: The students are occupying the university.

en: transfer (to another post or class); jemanden versetzen: stand someone up
why: ver = away: set a person somewhere else. "Stand someone up" is an idiom: learn it.
ex: Die Firma versetzt ihn nach Hamburg.
exEn: The company is transferring him to Hamburg.

why: Learn it as a word: er- does not mean "instead". The new part is set where the old one was.
exEn: We are replacing the old part.

en: take off (a lid); answer (the phone); lose weight
why: ab = off, down: take something off; your weight goes down.
exEn: I want to lose two kilos.

why: an = on, to you: take an offer on as yours.
exEn: I accept the offer.

why: auf = up: take sound up onto a recording; take someone up into a group.
exEn: We are recording the conversation.

why: ein = in: take it into your body, or into the till.
ex: Nehmen Sie die Tabletten nach dem Essen ein.
exEn: Take the tablets after the meal.

why: mit = along.
exEn: I will take you along.

en: sich etwas vornehmen: resolve, plan to do
why: vor = in front: take a task and put it in front of yourself.
ex: Ich nehme mir vor, jeden Tag zu lernen.
exEn: I have resolved to study every day.

why: zu = added.
exEn: The traffic is increasing.

en: take over; take on (costs, a task)
why: über = over: take something over from someone.
exEn: I will cover the costs.

why: Learn it as a word. Das Unternehmen = the company.
exEn: What shall we do at the weekend?

why: Learn it as a word.
exEn: He behaves well.

why: ent = out of: take something out of a source.
ex: Ihrer E-Mail entnehme ich, dass Sie kommen.
exEn: I gather from your email that you are coming.

why: ab = off, away: give it away from you.
ex: Ich gebe den Test um zehn ab.
exEn: I am handing in the test at ten.

why: an = on: give the details onto the form. "Show off" is a second sense to learn.
ex: Bitte geben Sie Ihre Adresse an.
exEn: Please give your address.

en: give up; post (a parcel); place (an ad)
why: auf = up: give it up (English uses the same picture). A parcel is given up at the counter.
exEn: Do not give up!

why: aus = out: the money goes out.
ex: Ich gebe zu viel Geld für Kaffee aus.
exEn: I spend too much money on coffee.

why: ein = in: give it into the machine.
exEn: Enter your password.

why: nach = behind: give way and fall in behind.
exEn: In the end he gives in.

why: zu = to, added: add an ingredient; give the point to the other person.
ex: Ich gebe zu, das war mein Fehler.
exEn: I admit that was my mistake.

why: um (unstressed) = all the way around.
exEn: Tall trees surround the house.

en: hand over; sich übergeben: be sick
why: über = over: give something over to someone.
ex: Der Vermieter übergibt uns die Schlüssel.
exEn: The landlord hands the keys over to us.

why: ver = away: a place that is given away is vergeben (taken). "Forgive" is a sense to learn.
exEn: The company is filling two posts.

en: result in; sich ergeben: arise; surrender
why: Learn it as a word. Das Ergebnis = the result.
exEn: That gives rise to a problem.

en: vom Weg abkommen: stray from the path
why: ab = off, away.
exEn: We are straying from the path.

en: arrive; es kommt darauf an: it depends
why: an = at: come to the place.
ex: Der Zug kommt um acht an.
exEn: The train arrives at eight.

en: come up, arise; für etwas aufkommen: pay for
why: auf = up: something comes up.
ex: Die Versicherung kommt für den Schaden auf.
exEn: The insurance pays for the damage.

en: get by (with money); get on (with someone)
why: aus = out, to the end: you come out at the end with enough.
exEn: We get on well with each other.

why: mit = along.
exEn: Are you coming along?

why: nach = after.
exEn: I will follow later.

why: vor = in front: something comes forward into view. Das kommt mir komisch vor = that seems odd to me.
exEn: These things happen.

why: Learn it as a word: um here does not mean around.
ex: Bei dem Unfall kam niemand um.
exEn: No one died in the accident.

why: durch = through to the other side.
ex: Mit Englisch kommt man hier gut durch.
exEn: You can get by here with English.

why: unter = under: get under a roof.
exEn: We are staying with friends.

why: Learn it as a word. It does not mean "become" (that is werden). A be- verb with an object: hat bekommen.
exEn: I get my result tomorrow.

why: ent = away from.
ex: Der Dieb entkommt durch das Fenster.
exEn: The thief escapes through the window.

en: concern; go on (a light); tackle (a problem)
why: an = at, toward: it comes at you, it concerns you. Das geht dich nichts an = that is none of your business.
exEn: That is none of your business.

why: auf = up, open.
ex: Die Sonne geht um sieben auf.
exEn: The sun rises at seven.

en: go out; run out; davon ausgehen: assume
why: aus = out.
exEn: We are going out tonight.

en: auf etwas eingehen: respond to; shrink (clothes); die (a plant)
why: ein = in: go into a question.
ex: Ich gehe gleich auf Ihre Frage ein.
exEn: I will come to your question in a moment.

why: nach = behind: a clock that goes behind the time.
ex: Meine Uhr geht fünf Minuten nach.
exEn: My watch is five minutes slow.

en: go ahead; be fast (a clock); proceed
why: vor = in front, ahead.
exEn: Go on ahead!

en: close (a door); auf jemanden zugehen: walk up to
why: zu = toward, shut.
exEn: The door will not shut.

why: durch = through.
ex: Wir gehen den Text noch einmal durch.
exEn: We are going through the text once more.

en: mit etwas umgehen: deal with, handle
why: um (stressed) = around: you move around something and handle it.
ex: Er geht gut mit Stress um.
exEn: He handles stress well.

why: um (unstressed) = all the way around, so you avoid it.
ex: Die neue Straße umgeht das Zentrum.
exEn: The new road bypasses the centre.

why: unter (stressed) = down below.
exEn: The sun is setting.

why: ver = away: time goes away. Die Vergangenheit = the past.
exEn: Time passes quickly.

why: Learn it as a word.
ex: Er hat einen schweren Fehler begangen.
exEn: He has made a serious mistake.

en: escape; be missed by (Das ist mir entgangen)
why: ent = away from: it goes away from you, so you miss it.
exEn: Many readers miss this detail.

en: put on (clothes); sich anziehen: get dressed; attract
why: an = on: pull clothes on.
exEn: I am getting dressed quickly.

why: aus = out. Move out: ist ausgezogen; take off clothes: hat ausgezogen.
exEn: We are moving out in May.

why: ein = in.
exEn: We are moving in next week.

why: um = change: change where you live, or what you wear. Move house: ist umgezogen; get changed: hat sich umgezogen.
exEn: We are moving to Leipzig.

why: ab = off.
ex: Die Firma zieht die Kosten vom Lohn ab.
exEn: The company deducts the costs from the wages.

en: bring up (a child); wind up (a clock)
why: auf = up: pull a child up to adulthood.
ex: Sie zieht drei Kinder allein auf.
exEn: She is bringing up three children on her own.

why: vor = in front: pull one option to the front.
exEn: I prefer tea.

why: zu = shut.
exEn: I am closing the curtains.

why: über (unstressed) = over: go over the limit.
exEn: I never overdraw my account.

why: über (stressed) = over: pull a jacket on over your clothes.
exEn: Put a jacket on!

en: sich beziehen auf: refer to; das Bett beziehen: put sheets on
why: Learn it as a word. In a letter: Ich beziehe mich auf Ihre Anzeige.
ex: Ich beziehe mich auf Ihre Anzeige.
exEn: I am writing about your advertisement.

why: er = to a result: pull a child up to adulthood.
exEn: She is bringing her children up bilingual.

en: pull out of shape (das Gesicht); spoil (a child)
why: ver = off course: pulled out of its shape. Not the same verb as verzeihen (forgive).
exEn: He pulls a face.

why: ent = away from.
ex: Das Gericht entzieht ihm den Führerschein.
exEn: The court is taking his licence away.

why: auf = up: something pops up into view.
ex: Mir fällt auf, dass du müde bist.
exEn: I notice that you are tired.

why: aus = out: a lesson drops out of the timetable.
exEn: The class is cancelled today.

why: ein = in: an idea falls into your head.
exEn: I cannot think of an example.

why: um = over.
exEn: The vase is about to fall over.

why: durch = through: fall through the net.
exEn: I hope I do not fail.

why: zu = shut.
exEn: The door swings shut.

why: über = over: fall upon someone.
exEn: Two men are robbing the bank.

en: please: Das gefällt mir = I like it
why: Learn it as a word. Its participle is the same as fallen's, but it takes haben: hat gefallen.
exEn: I like the flat.

why: ent = away from: the name fell away from you.
exEn: The fee is waived.

why: ver = away, used up.
ex: Der Gutschein verfällt Ende des Jahres.
exEn: The voucher expires at the end of the year.

why: zer = to pieces.
exEn: The old paper is falling apart.

why: ab = away: hold someone away from something.
ex: Der Lärm hält mich vom Lernen ab.
exEn: The noise keeps me from studying.

why: an = at: the bus holds at the stop.
ex: Der Bus hält hier nicht an.
exEn: The bus does not stop here.

en: hold up, delay; sich aufhalten: stay
why: auf = up: hold someone up (English uses the same picture).
exEn: The traffic jam is holding us up.

why: aus = out, to the end: hold out.
ex: Ich halte die Hitze nicht aus.
exEn: I cannot stand the heat.

why: ein = in: stay inside the limits.
exEn: We are keeping to the deadline.

why: durch = through to the end.
exEn: Hang in there!

why: be- aims at a target: hold on to it as yours. The participle is behalten.
exEn: I am keeping the book.

why: Learn it as a word.
exEn: He is behaving strangely.

why: Learn it as a word. Formal for bekommen.
ex: Sie erhalten die Unterlagen per Post.
exEn: You will receive the documents by post.

why: Learn it as a word.
exEn: The drink contains a lot of sugar.

why: Learn it as a word.
exEn: We are chatting about music.

why: ab = done, settled: talk until it is settled.
ex: Wir sprechen den Termin vorher ab.
exEn: We agree the date beforehand.

why: an = toward: speak toward a person or a topic.
ex: Sie spricht das Problem direkt an.
exEn: She raises the problem directly.

why: aus = out: speak it out.
exEn: How do you pronounce that?

why: nach = after.
exEn: Please repeat after me.

why: zu = to: speak courage to someone.
exEn: She encourages me.

why: durch = through.
ex: Wir sprechen den Plan noch einmal durch.
exEn: We are talking the plan through once more.

why: be- aims at a target: über etwas sprechen → etwas besprechen.
exEn: We will discuss that tomorrow.

why: Learn "promise" as a word. sich versprechen (misspeak) is ver- = wrong, like sich verschreiben and sich verhören.
exEn: I promise you.

why: Learn it as a word.
exEn: That does not match my expectations.

why: wider = against: speak against.
exEn: I disagree with you there.

why: ab = off, from a source.
exEn: He copies the homework.

why: an = toward a person.
ex: Ich schreibe die Firma direkt an.
exEn: I am writing to the company directly.

why: auf = onto paper.
ex: Ich schreibe mir die Nummer auf.
exEn: I am writing down the number.

en: advertise (a job); write out in full
why: aus = out in public: a post written out for everyone.
ex: Die Firma schreibt die Stelle aus.
exEn: The company is advertising the post.

why: ein = in: write your name into the list. Das Einschreiben = a registered letter.
ex: Ich schreibe mich für den Kurs ein.
exEn: I am enrolling on the course.

why: mit = along: write along while someone speaks.
exEn: I take notes in class.

why: vor = before: written down before anyone acts.
ex: Das Gesetz schreibt eine Pause vor.
exEn: The law requires a break.

why: um (stressed) = change: write it again differently.
exEn: I am rewriting the text.

why: um (unstressed) = all the way around: write around a word you do not know.
ex: Wenn mir ein Wort nicht einfällt, umschreibe ich es.
exEn: If I cannot think of a word, I describe it in other words.

why: unter = under: write your name under the text.
exEn: Please sign here.

why: be- aims at a target: write about something → describe it.
exEn: Describe the picture.

en: prescribe (medicine); sich verschreiben: make a slip of the pen
why: sich verschreiben is ver- = wrong. "Prescribe" is a sense to learn.
ex: Der Arzt verschreibt mir ein Medikament.
exEn: The doctor prescribes me some medicine.

en: sich etwas ansehen: look at, watch
why: an = toward.
ex: Ich sehe mir den Film an.
exEn: I am watching the film.

why: auf = up.
exEn: She looks up from her book.

why: aus = out: how you look from the outside.
exEn: You look tired.

why: ein = in: see into something until you get it.
exEn: I accept my mistake.

why: nach = after, following up: you look into something afterwards to check it.
exEn: I am looking it up in the dictionary.

why: vor = before: seen in advance.
ex: Der Plan sieht eine Pause vor.
exEn: The plan includes a break.

why: zu = toward.
ex: Ich sehe dir beim Kochen zu.
exEn: I am watching you cook.

why: um = around.
exEn: I am just looking around.

why: durch = through.
exEn: I am looking through the documents.

why: über = over: your eyes pass over it and miss it.
exEn: I often miss small mistakes.

why: ab = away.
ex: Der Zug fährt um acht ab.
exEn: The train leaves at eight.

why: ein = in.
ex: Der Zug fährt auf Gleis drei ein.
exEn: The train is arriving at platform three.

why: mit = along.
exEn: Are you coming with us?

why: durch = through.
exEn: The train does not stop here.

why: um (stressed) = over: drive into it so it falls over.
ex: Fahr bitte die Mülltonne nicht um!
exEn: Please do not knock the bin over!

why: um (unstressed) = all the way around.
exEn: We are driving around the traffic jam.

why: über = over.
exEn: He runs a red light.

why: be- aims at a target: the road becomes the object.
exEn: Many lorries use this road.

why: History: erfahren first meant "reach by travelling, explore". What you find on the way is what you learn. As an adjective: experienced.
exEn: When will you find out the result?

why: ver = off course. Same pattern: sich verlaufen (on foot).
ex: Ohne Navi verfahre ich mich immer.
exEn: Without satnav I always get lost.

why: auf = up.
exEn: I get up at seven.

why: aus = to the end: endure it to the end.
exEn: I cannot stand him.

en: pass (an exam); bestehen aus: consist of
why: be- aims at a target: you stand your ground against the exam. "Consist of" is a sense to learn.
exEn: I pass the exam.

why: Learn it as a word.
exEn: I do not understand the question.

why: ent = coming into being: something comes to stand.
exEn: That is how many problems arise.

why: Learn it as a word. Hat gestanden can mean "stood" or "confessed".
exEn: The culprit confesses everything.

why: über = over: stand until it is over.
exEn: We will get through this week too.

why: wider = against.
exEn: I resist the chocolate.
